from solution import subject_marks


def test_issue_example():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda as in the given example."""
    result = subject_marks([('English', 88), ('Science', 90), ('Maths', 97), ('Social sciences', 82)])
    expected = [('Social sciences', 82), ('English', 88), ('Science', 90), ('Maths', 97)]  # 82 < 88 < 90 < 97
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_empty_list():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda handles an empty list."""
    result = subject_marks([])
    expected = []  # 0 == 0 items to order
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_single_tuple():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda with a single tuple stays the same."""
    result = subject_marks([('Maths', 75)])
    expected = [('Maths', 75)]  # 75 == 75 single item
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_already_sorted():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda keeps an already sorted list."""
    result = subject_marks([('English', 10), ('Science', 20), ('Maths', 30)])
    expected = [('English', 10), ('Science', 20), ('Maths', 30)]  # 10 < 20 < 30
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_reverse_sorted():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda reverses descending marks to ascending."""
    result = subject_marks([('Maths', 97), ('Science', 90), ('English', 88)])
    expected = [('English', 88), ('Science', 90), ('Maths', 97)]  # 88 < 90 < 97
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_duplicate_marks():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda orders marks with duplicates."""
    result = subject_marks([('English', 85), ('Science', 85), ('Maths', 70)])
    expected_marks = [70, 85, 85]  # 70 < 85 == 85
    assert [m for _, m in result] == expected_marks


def test_issue_boundary_marks():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda handles boundary marks 0 and 100."""
    result = subject_marks([('Science', 100), ('English', 0), ('Maths', 50)])
    expected = [('English', 0), ('Maths', 50), ('Science', 100)]  # 0 < 50 < 100
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_five_elements():
    """Sort a list of tuples using lambda with five unsorted tuples."""
    result = subject_marks([('English', 88), ('Science', 90), ('Maths', 97), ('Social sciences', 82), ('Hindi', 75)])
    expected = [('Hindi', 75), ('Social sciences', 82), ('English', 88), ('Science', 90), ('Maths', 97)]  # 75 < 82 < 88 < 90 < 97
    assert result == expected


def test_contract_sorted_ascending():
    """Contract: 'sort a list of tuples' orders by marks ascending."""
    result = subject_marks([('Physics', 60), ('Chemistry', 55), ('Biology', 65)])
    expected = [('Chemistry', 55), ('Physics', 60), ('Biology', 65)]  # 55 < 60 < 65
    assert result == expected


def test_contract_pairs_preserved():
    """Contract: 'sort a list of tuples' keeps each subject-mark pair intact."""
    result = subject_marks([('Maths', 40), ('English', 30), ('Science', 50)])
    expected_set = {('Maths', 40), ('English', 30), ('Science', 50)}  # 30 < 40 < 50 intact pairs
    assert set(result) == expected_set
